clue.text: Step down first of stairs to break rule

indicators.note: one thing breaking another splits it open, so the letter sits inside the word for rule

parts.note: to rule is to reign; as a noun, a monarch's reign is their rule

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word stairs

explanation.surface: Someone coming down a staircase trips on the first step and breaks a household rule.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand down from a post is to quit it formally, a synonym of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Upper house covering little Australian paperwork

parts.note: roo is the short form of kangaroo, an Australian animal
the paper is the FT, the Financial Times
the work is OP, short for opus

explanation.surface: The upper house of parliament is covering an Australian's paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upper house' looks like a parliamentary chamber, but read together with 'covering' it is the top of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The top of a building's covering is its highest outer surface.

clue.text: Dog or worm is up an instrument

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a rat, like a dog or worm, is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A puzzle about whether a dog or worm can play music.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked Indian plucked string instrument.

clue.text: No thanks to Garbo, Monroe wandering in space backstage

indicators.note: no in front of the thanks word means it is dropped from the name

parts.note: Greta Garbo, the Swedish film star
ta is British informal for thanks

indicators.note: wandering means the letters roam into a new order

explanation.surface: Garbo is snubbed while Monroe drifts about in the space behind the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: GRETA loses TA to give GRE; MONROE rearranged by 'wandering' gives ENROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Performers wait in this lounge off-stage before going on.

clue.text: Having turned back nearly half way across ocean, explorer leaves from the Americas

indicators.note: turning back means the whole run of letters is read in the opposite direction
half way across the six-letter word ocean is its first three letters; nearly drops one more, leaving two

parts.note: John Cabot, the Venetian navigator who sailed to North America for England in 1497

explanation.surface: An explorer turns his ship back mid-Atlantic and sails away from the New World.
explanation.walkthrough: OC (the first two letters of 'ocean') plus CABOT, the whole lot reversed by 'Having turned back', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco is a plant native to the Americas whose dried leaves are smoked.

clue.text: Current king in approach to palace, scratching bottom

indicators.note: in places the king letter inside the shortened road name
scratching the bottom drops the final letter, the last in a down clue

parts.note: The Mall is the London avenue leading to Buckingham Palace
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A present-day king scratches his backside on the road to the palace.
explanation.walkthrough: THE MALL loses its last L to 'scratching bottom', and R goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermal is a rising current of warm air used by gliders and birds.

clue.text: Curry from Lithuania? Not quite!

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short by its last letter

parts.note: Lithuania is one of the Baltic states, so things from there are Baltic

explanation.surface: Asking whether a curry comes from Lithuania, and being told not quite.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a spiced dish cooked and served in a wok-like pan, made popular in Birmingham.

clue.text: Nation supporting lead player in Chad every so often

parts.note: a co-star is a performer sharing top billing with the lead

indicators.note: every so often picks every other letter of the words

explanation.surface: A country backs a leading performer in Chad from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: The Central American republic is a sovereign country.

clue.text: Port, after lid removed, passed round the wrong way

parts.note: a round thing is O-shaped

indicators.note: the wrong way means the letters are read backwards
the lid of a word is its top, its first letter in a down clue

parts.note: taken as written before the cut

explanation.surface: A bottle of port passed the wrong way round the table once uncorked.
explanation.walkthrough: PASSED loses P to give ASSED, which 'the wrong way' turns into DESSA. Port is passed clockwise at British dinners.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea port in Ukraine.

clue.text: Thug eating up junket for starters — it's coated in breadcrumbs

indicators.note: eating means the thug word swallows the letters inside it

parts.note: a goon is a hired thug

indicators.note: for starters takes the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A thug wolfs down a pudding as starters before something breaded.
explanation.definitionFit: A goujon is a strip of fish or chicken fried in breadcrumbs.

clue.text: Where glasses sit precisely

definitions.meaning: spectacles rest on the bridge of the face, literally on that feature
as an idiom meaning exactly right, as a bet landing spot-on

explanation.surface: A description of spectacles perched exactly in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles rest literally on that facial feature, and the idiom means exactly or spot-on.

clue.text: Thread attaching fringes of lungi and shawl to back of cape

indicators.note: the fringes of each word are its outermost letters, first and last
the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A tailor stitches the fringed edges of a lungi and a shawl onto a cape.
explanation.walkthrough: A lungi is a sarong-like wrap worn in South Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, strong cotton yarn, used especially for stockings.

clue.text: Shroud city featuring shrouds

indicators.note: a word that shrouds another wraps it from view, so the city lies concealed inside featuring

explanation.surface: A city whose claim to fame is its burial cloths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrouds' looks like a repeat of the burial cloth, but it is the verb, covering up a run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Piedmont capital's cathedral houses the famous linen relic said to bear Christ's image.

clue.text: Islanders on Martinique not once seizing vessel

indicators.note: one word seizing another grips it inside itself

parts.note: Martinique is French-speaking, and the French for never is jamais
a can is a container or vessel

explanation.surface: Caribbean islanders on a neighbouring island who have never once grabbed a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not once' looks like a negative remark, but 'on Martinique' asks for it in French.
explanation.definitionFit: People from the Caribbean island nation are its natives, so they are islanders.

clue.text: Snack, Spooner's filth of the filth?

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words, after the Rev Spooner

parts.note: the filth is British slang for the police, so a cop
filth here is obscene material, porn

explanation.surface: A smutty question about a snack belonging to the police's dirty material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filth of the filth' gives COP PORN (the police's smut); swapping the opening letters gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Popped maize kernels are a classic cinema nibble.

clue.text: Earth, say, on English sycamore

parts.note: Earth is an example of a planet
re means on or about

explanation.surface: The sycamore declared the English tree of the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: In North America the sycamore is a plane tree.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage the sycamore is a species of plane, a tree of genus Platanus.

clue.text: See 27
Setter with water living on fruit

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the living piece above the fruit

parts.note: quick is old English for living, as in the quick and the dead
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A crossword setter, given water, survives on fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword compiler, but it is something that sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Calcium oxide reacts with water and hardens, so it acts as a setting agent in mortar.

clue.text: Compassion some weeks after conflict

indicators.note: after places the weeks piece behind the conflict piece

parts.note: war is armed conflict
a month, abbreviated MTH, is a span of some weeks

explanation.surface: Kindness returns a few weeks after a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmth of feeling is kindly sympathy, a figurative synonym.

clue.text: Fool Oscar but not Wilde?

parts.note: the first half of the name Oscar Wilde, a famous wit, is Oscar without Wilde

explanation.surface: Calling someone named Oscar a fool, while insisting he is not the writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar without Wilde is half the name of a famous wit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimwitted person is a fool, a dictionary synonym.

clue.text: Some leaves to make cha?

parts.note: spin the letters A C H around and they make cha

explanation.surface: A question about tea leaves and how to brew a cup of cha.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha is British slang for tea, which makes 'leaves' look like tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable is eaten for its dark green leaves.

clue.text: Most painful? Then put your feet up

parts.note: so means then, as in 'so, what next?'
to put your feet up is to rest

explanation.surface: Advice for someone in great pain: then lie back and relax.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of sore means aching the most.

clue.text: Somewhere dangerous, exciting to see

parts.note: hot means exciting, as in a hot tip
to spot is to see

explanation.surface: A dangerous place that is thrilling to visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A trouble area of conflict or danger, as in a world flashpoint.

clue.text: Rash appearing as potty put on head

parts.note: potty is British slang for crazy
a cap is something put on the head

explanation.surface: A skin rash that shows up as a toddler's potty is placed on someone's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Madcap means reckless or impulsive, a synonym for rash as an adjective.

clue.text: Like viruses having a rest, lying back inside maple

indicators.note: inside places the rest piece within the maple word

parts.note: Acer is the botanical genus of maples

indicators.note: lying back means those letters are laid in reverse order

parts.note: a lull is a pause or rest

explanation.surface: Viruses taking a breather, reclining in a maple tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying back' reverses A plus the rest word to give LLULA; Acer is the botanical name for maples.
explanation.definitionFit: Viruses are not made of cells, so biologists describe them as non-cellular.

clue.text: Contract required while in shelter

indicators.note: in places the while word inside the shelter word

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side
as means while, as in 'as I was leaving'

explanation.surface: An agreement needed while sheltering somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A rental agreement for property is a legal contract.

clue.text: Tidy, maintained without muck for a start

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the kept word goes round the letter

parts.note: maintained means kept, as a garden is kept

indicators.note: for a start takes the opening letter of muck

explanation.surface: A tidy home, maintained with no muck at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like it means minus, but here it is the old sense 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kempt, the rarer partner of unkempt, means neatly groomed.

clue.text: Old document, Reform Act (anagram)

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A historic document, the Reform Act, is labelled an anagram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reform Act' looks like the 1832 law; 'Reform' rearranges ACT plus ANAGRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1215 charter sealed by King John is a famous medieval English text.

clue.text: See 25
Fairy, perhaps, raised just over half a ton of cash to support tree strangled by branch

indicators.note: to support places the following pieces after the first part, holding it up
strangled by means the tree is gripped inside the branch word

parts.note: a wing is a branch of a building or organisation
the ash is a common tree
raised means up
a ton is 100; just over half is 51, LI in Roman numerals
quid is British slang for a pound

explanation.surface: A fairy raises funds to support a tree being choked by a branch.
explanation.walkthrough: Fairy is a British brand of dish soap; QUID is a pound, so 'cash'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairy is a leading UK brand of dish soap, an example of the product.

clue.text: Stop propaganda happening

parts.note: PR, public relations, is a polite word for propaganda
an event is a happening

explanation.surface: A call to halt propaganda that is going on.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent something is to stop it from happening, a synonym.

clue.text: The wrong way for TV presenters to pour wine

indicators.note: the wrong way round for the duo means their two names swap places from the usual billing

parts.note: Ant and Dec are a British TV presenting duo; here Dec comes first
the other half of the duo, Ant, now comes second

explanation.surface: Pouring wine is said to be the wrong way for TV hosts to behave.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a famous British TV presenting double act, always billed in that order.
explanation.definitionFit: To decant wine is to pour it from its bottle into another vessel.
